When to create a variant

Variant use

Create a variant if you need multiple versions of a component with shared properties. This allows users to switch between the variants.


The most common use cases we use variants for are:

Component type
e.g. Primary/Secondary/Outline/Ghost Button
Component variant
e.g. Standard/Icon only Button
Component size
e.g. Small/Large Button
Component state
e.g. Standard/Pressed/Hovered/Focused


Variant sets

Some components require multiple sets of variants to distinguish between component variants, types, sizes and states.

Component type is used to describe a component specific function or use case, e.g. primary button vs secondary button.
Component variant is used to describe visual changes or other minor differences, e.g. standard button vs icon only button.
Component size is used to describe size changes, e.g. small button vs large button.
Component state is used to describe interactive state changes, e.g. standard state vs hovered state


warning  Best practice
When to use a boolean property

Use a boolean property to hide or show elements within a component. This helps reduce the number of component variants.



warning  Best practice
When to use instance swap

Use instance swaps for flexible components with undetermined content.


This could be a content slot that can be replaced with any content, or an icon that can be swapped with another icon.



warning  Best practice
When to use the text property

Use the text property to indicate which text layers should be editable.

Avoid conflicting component layer properties

Component layers cannot have position sticky and position absolute at the same time.

Organising properties – property type

How to order properties

Organise properties based on the order they appear on your component, following the sequence:

Variant
Boolean
Instance swap
Text

Group variant properties together and add them at the top of the component properties panel.



How to order Instance swaps and Text properties

Instance swaps and text properties are treated differently.


If an Instance swap or text property is linked to a boolean property, group them together.



How to order properties in complex components

When deciding on the property order in complex components, base it on the order they appear in the component.



warning  Best practice
Organising properties – use case

How to order variants

Organise multiple variants based on the most used/relevant properties in the layout.

Type
Variant
Size
State


For example, place a state property below a type propert


The state property is rarely used outside of prototyping, and it is less frequently used when designing for real-world products in Figma.



warning  Best practice
Nested properties

How to expose nested properties

When creating a new component, if you are using instances of a different component inside it, you can choose to expose and include the properties of the instances in your new component properties panel.


For example, the Avatar component is using instances of the Badge component inside it. When creating its properties, you get the option to expose the nested instance properties through the properties panel.



When to expose nested properties

Nested properties are treated differently for each component, based on its complexity.


As a general rule, we try to expose as many properties as needed and allow the designer to delve deeper into the component to manage properties for each atom or subcomponent.


For more complex components, only expose the absolutely necessary properties.


For example, in the Flyout menu component we only expose the absolutely necessary properties. To access properties for individual elements, such as the Menu list items, you will need to select the specific subcomponent through the layer panel.
